real_estate.homebuilder: Builder confidence fell to 25, the lowest since April 2012; here, brand new homes have lost their edge over resale.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.46% this morning, down 0.02 from Tuesday, with the 15-year at 6.98%. On today's $1,288,500 Fremont median with 20% down, that is about $7,179 a month in principal and interest.

Builder confidence fell four points to 25 in November, the lowest since April 2012, according to the NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (chart). 46% of builders cut prices, the most since the pandemic, by an average of 6%, and 68% offered incentives. In the West, which includes California, the three month reading fell to 23, the weakest of the four regions.

Census figures out this morning show single family permits fell 8.7% in October to a 772,000 annual pace, which NAHB calls the slowest since January 2023. Starts rose, but within the survey's margin of error.

Here, the edge brand new homes had over resale is gone. In our five cities, 10 of 42 homes built in 2025 or 2026 are in contract (24%), the same rate as resale; on October 20 it was 19 of 52 (37%). Across the Bay East board, 21 of 136 new homes are in contract (15%), against 25% for resale.

Wednesday's export shows 2,350 board wide, from 2,381 Tuesday, with 132 coming soon and 119 brand new. The five city ledger is 594, from 604: Fremont (200) fell five, Hayward (172) four, and Milpitas (95) and Union City (56) one each, while Newark (71) added one.

What this means for you: buyers, a builder with finished homes to move is negotiating, so ask for a rate buydown or closing costs before a price cut. Sellers, nearby new construction is competing with incentives, so price to today's comps.

• Board wide: 2,350 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 132 coming soon and 119 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 594 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 530 are on the market and 64 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 200 live, 160 active, 24 coming soon and 15 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,288,500 at $783 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 40 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 172, Milpitas 95, Newark 71, Union City 56.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,048,371 at $668 a square foot. 259 homes are priced under a million, and 189 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.news:
Tuesday's close: the S&P 500 fell 1.03%, the Dow 1.64% and the Nasdaq 0.74%. At 10:25 AM PT Wednesday the S&P was down 0.05%, the Dow down 0.85% and the Nasdaq up 0.51%.

Santa Clara's Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue for the quarter ended October 25, up 103% from a year ago, and guided to about $130 billion for the current quarter, its first report since Jensen Huang stepped down, with finance chief Colette Kress serving as interim CEO. The stock slipped 0.44% Tuesday and was down 2.15% at $152.11 this morning. Doubling sales was not enough to move the needle.

economy.note: Cards are Tuesday's settlements: the 10-Year from Treasury, gold and silver December COMEX futures, Brent ICE front month. Wednesday's moves are in the text.
economy.commentary:
Political advertisers spent a record $12.06 billion in the 2025 to 2026 cycle, according to AdImpact, the first midterm cycle to outspend a presidential one ($11.20 billion in 2024) (chart). California led every state at $1.32 billion, the first state ever past $1 billion in a single cycle, and broadcast TV took the biggest share, $5.85 billion. Local stations had a good fall.

Retail sales rose 0.2% in October after 0.8% in September, the Census Bureau reported, a gain too small to rule out no change at all.

The 10-Year Treasury closed Tuesday at 5.10%, down 0.02; the newsletter printed 5.13% and up. Gold settled Tuesday at $3,864.20 and silver at $47.36, the newsletter's $3,850 gold being an evening quote. Both are sliding this morning: gold down 3.21% near $3,740.30 and silver down 5.11% near $44.94. Brent settled at $93.14 (the newsletter said $93.49) and is down about 2.2% near $91.11.

feature_image.alt: Bar chart, total U.S. political ad spending by election cycle from AdImpact: 2022 midterm $8.90 billion, 2024 presidential $11.20 billion, 2026 midterm $12.06 billion, up 8% on 2024. Local panel: California $1.32 billion in 2025 to 2026, the most of any state and the first ever past $1 billion; Texas next at $1.13 billion.
feature_image.caption: This cycle's political ad spending set a record, and California led every state.
feature_image.source: AdImpact, as reported by CNBC (Nov. 17, 2026), TheWrap and Campaigns & Elections
